#317 Studio: the system map view — fog, live agents, broken laws, history, and seen (#306)
merged 2026-11-22T16:22:20Z

## Summary

The **Map view** (spec #306, project 2 of 4): Studio draws `system-map.json` from `origin`'s default branch, with fog, live agents, broken laws, part history, a shared **Seen** gate and always-on stop rules.

```text
src-tauri/src/
├── map.rs          # map from origin/HEAD, fetch cooldown + lock, map-state.json (positions, tiers), live-agent placement
├── fog.rs          # first-parent walk, thin/thick by union of parent+commit maps, effective tier, "I know this"
├── ci_laws.rs      # latest finished studio.yml run via gh, nextest/Node failure parsing → @law test names → parts; ci-last.json
├── history.rs      # a part's first-parent commits since the map's birth, map at a commit, commit files/diff
└── stop_rules.rs   # stop-rules.jsonl event log, facts for the evaluator
system-map/src/     # touched_for_map (in memory), parse_lenient, law_tests / test_name_after
ui/
├── seen.ts         # watchSeen: ≥50% element or viewport, 500 ms, visible + focused, active view
├── map.ts, map-model.ts           # shell, plates, drag (6 px), auto-place, layered Esc
├── map-sheet.ts, map-drawer.ts    # part sheet (tier, laws, fog, I know this, CI, history), read-only drawer
├── map-agents.ts, map-history.ts  # chips + not placed; strip + scrub
└── stop-rules.ts   # thresholds, one-time review (Map view + Home fallback)
```

```text
Esc in the Map view
  drawer open      → close drawer
  scrubbed         → back to now
  sheet open       → close sheet
  else             → leave Map view
```

The Esc order follows ticket #313 (drawer before scrubbed); the spec's two lines disagree with each other — a one-line change in `ui/map-model.ts` `layerOrder` if the spec's order is wanted.

Per ticket: #307 Seen helper, story-rail cards fixed · #308 system-map entry points · #309 shell, plates, drag, empty state · #310 fog, part sheet, Home mark · #311 live agents · #312 broken laws, drawer · #313 history strip · #314 stop rules, `behaviour/map.md`.

## Evidence

Snap screenshots (`local-evidence/project-2-map-view/screenshots/`, compared with Treatment C `C-busy.png`):

- `309-mapCalm.png`, `309-mapEmpty.png` — calm map; no-map empty state with "Draft a map"
- `final-map-fog.png` (= `310-map-busy.png`) — thin + thick mist, part sheet open; `310-home-mark.png`
- `311-map-busy.png` — chips on parts, "needs you" pill, not placed list
- `312-mapBroken.png`, `312-mapProof.png`, `312-mapBrokenLog.png` — broken-law mark beside Needs you; proof and CI-log drawers
- `313-mapScrubbed.png` — scrubbed to a past commit, "Viewing … · Back to now"
- `314-review-map.png`, `314-review-home.png` — the one-time review, no counts

- **Before:** story-rail cards were marked shown when built in the DOM; no Map view.
  **After:** `npm run check` green (Rust nextest, 627 node tests, `system-map check`, wire types); `npm run snap:all` renders 75 fixtures. New tests include:

```text
fog:      first open starts clear; paths move fogs both parts thick; zone/ignored/tier → no fog;
          overlapping walks file nothing twice and don't undo "I know this"
ci_laws:  tagged test fails → its part; unrelated test in same file → nothing; fmt fails → not-run;
          real nextest ids (studio-core::it wire::…, studio::bin/studio …) match their tags
seen:     off-screen / unfocused / folded rail / behind the Map view → not shown; tall card at 50% viewport → shown
stop:     no review before 14 active days AND 20 merged PRs; Home review only when the Map view missed
```

## Review

Final review: standards, spec and correctness passes over the whole branch, plus a re-review of the fix commits. Fixed: fog lost update, merge hook blocking the landed loop and firing on start, out-of-order scrub results, locks not freed on panic, torn stop-rule line, CI result lost on restart, per-project merged-PR start, Home learning items on Seen, stale banner/sheet after switching to a no-map project, missing-tier default, `development.md`, redundant dev dependency, review banner snap fixtures, mist too faint, sheet clipping plates.

## Outside review

Model: gemini-4-neon-medium.

- **Round 1** — cost: 4.4 min, 324916 tokens; Gemini quota left: weekly 79% to 77%, 5h 95% to 90%
  1. `holds` never matched this workspace's `it` test binaries — **fixed**; not reported by the correctness pass.
  2. TAP parser index out of bounds on a duplicate title — **fixed**; not reported by the correctness pass.
  3. Merged PRs 0 for a project never opened, so Home's fallback never came due — **fixed**; the spec pass reported the counting basis, not this case.
  4. Home mark watched a node `patch` discards — **fixed**; not reported.
  5. Focus on Home didn't redraw marks — **fixed**; not reported.
  6. Story-rail cards counted as seen behind the Map view — **fixed**; not reported.
  7. Home quizzes counted as seen behind the Map view — **fixed**; not reported.
- **Round 2** (`--since 9230b635b`) — cost: 4.3 min, 292996 tokens; Gemini quota left: weekly 77% to 76%, 5h 90% to 86%
  1. "Back to now" a no-op on an unreadable past map — **fixed**; not reported.
  2. `rail_shown` still told true behind the Map view — **fixed**; not reported.
  3. `studio::bin/studio` unit-test ids never matched — **fixed**; not reported.
  4. Home mark not counted on later days while Studio stays open — **fixed**; not reported.

## Left out or limited

- "Not yet ratified" on laws: no ratification field exists yet (project 3).
- CI workflow is the constant `studio.yml` (plotkeeper only, per the spec's scope).
- Active days are Studio-wide, as the spec defines them; merged PRs count per project from that project's first event.
- A merge that lands while Studio is closed starts no fetch; the next map open fetches.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

New data-folder files (`map-state.json`, `ci-last.json`, `stop-rules.jsonl`) are additive and tolerant of missing/older shapes; story-rail `shown` timestamps are not rewritten, but what counts as shown changes from now on (one-time step in weekly guess rates, accepted in #306).

**Blast Radius:** moderate

Touches the story rail's shown path, Home's rows and learning `shown`, `refresh_landed` (merge hook on its own thread), and runs `git fetch` / `gh run` on map open and focus (cooldown-guarded). After merge, quit Studio and run `npm run start` from the main checkout.

=== SPEC ===
#306 Studio: Spec: the system map view — fog, live agents, broken laws, history, and seen
created 2026-11-22T13:11:20Z
(trimmed to its user stories and implementation decisions)

## User Stories

1. As Daniel, I want to open a project's Map view from the palette (`studio::ShowMap`), a rebindable key, or a quiet mark on Home's project row, so that I can reach the map without hunting for it.
2. As Daniel, I want the Map view to take the story rail and terminal column together while keeping the session list and top bar live, so that the map has generous room without blinding me to `Needs you` sessions across projects.
3. As Daniel, I want to switch between projects from the project name at the top-left of the Map view, so that I can inspect any project's map without leaving the view.
4. As Daniel, I want clicking any session in the session list, clicking empty list space (Home), pressing the map key again, or pressing Esc to leave the Map view cleanly, so that returning to my work is effortless.
5. As Daniel, I want Esc inside the Map view to be layered — first returning from a scrubbed historical commit to live, then closing an open part sheet or drill-down drawer, then leaving the Map view — so that Esc never throws me out of the map unexpectedly.
6. As Daniel, I want parts drawn as clean plates with their name, short caption, and law marks (distinct between backed by a check and on trust), with links drawn rim to rim and outside actors placed cleanly, so that the map feels like a pilot's cockpit rather than a Mermaid flowchart.
7. As Daniel, I want every part to keep its saved position per part id in the studio's data folder and never reshuffle on reload, so that I build lasting spatial memory of my system.
8. As Daniel, I want to drag a part plate (past a ~5–6 px threshold so normal clicks never nudge it) to adjust its saved position, so that I can fix an awkward auto-placement without needing a layout editor.
9. As Daniel, I want a newly added part to be placed near the parts it links to (in its declared `zone` when present) without moving existing parts, so that the map grows without breaking my spatial memory.
10. As Daniel, I want the Map view, fog, and broken laws to all read from `origin`'s default branch as last fetched (`origin/HEAD`), so that the map never contradicts CI or waits on me remembering to pull `main`.
11. As Daniel, I want fog rendered as a cool-grey mist (`--mist`) that stays readable over a plate while keeping the part's name at full strength, so that it reads as "unknown" rather than "disabled" or "selected" and stays distinct by temperature from warm focus/brief light.
12. As Daniel, I want fog to have two deterministic strengths — thin for internal file changes and thick for changes to a part's laws, links, or flows in `system-map.json` — and never scale by commit or PR count, so that fog reflects mental-model drift rather than a nagging backlog.
13. As Daniel, I want every project's map to start clear at my first open of its Map view, so that every mist I see represents a real change that landed after I started using the map.
14. As Daniel, I want to change a part's tier (`Core`, `Interface-only`, `Black box`) directly inside its part sheet, persisted in the studio's data folder, and never be nudged to lower a tier, so that I stay in control of what I track.
15. As Daniel, I want Black box parts never to fog and Interface-only parts to fog only on thick (edge/law/flow) changes, so that my attention stays on what I care about.
16. As Daniel, I want a quiet **"I know this"** button on a fogged part's sheet that clears that part's fog (with a smooth mist-lift reveal) and records the clear separately in stop-rule tracking, so that I can clear fog before PR briefs exist or when I already understand a change.
17. As Daniel, I want to see live `Running` and `Needs you` sessions and Workers placed as chips on every part their active turn has changed files in — with `Needs you` keeping its loud orange pill and clicking any chip jumping to that session — so that I can see what agents are changing right now.
18. As Daniel, I want read-only Helpers and finished (`Your turn`, `Idle`, `Ended`) sessions to leave the map immediately, and active sessions with no changed files yet, `turn_trees: false` (`agy`), status-only sessions (`Codex`), or `ignored`-only edits to sit in a quiet **not placed** list beside the map, so that no active session vanishes and finished work never clutters the map.
19. As Daniel, I want Studio to check CI on the default branch via `gh` when the Map view opens, when the window gains focus while it is open, and when a merge to the default branch is seen (never on a timer), so that broken laws stay accurate without background polling.
20. As Daniel, I want a broken-law mark (*"a test that backs laws here failed on main"*) to appear only when the specific test function tagged with `@law:` actually failed in that CI run — never when an unrelated test in the same file fails, or when formatting/clippy/build fails or the log is unreadable — and I want the drill-down to distinguish *"passed"* from *"law tests did not run"*, so that loud colour never cries wolf.
21. As Daniel, I want a part's sheet to show its plain description, tier selector, laws (marked backed by a check or on trust, plus "not yet ratified" where applicable), fog status, and a scrubbable history strip of first-parent commits on `origin/HEAD` from the map's birth onward, so that I can inspect a part's evolution.
22. As Daniel, I want scrubbing a part's history strip to render the map as of that historical commit (read-only, with live agents and CI hidden and a quiet *"Viewing `<commit>` · Back to now"* banner), so that I can see how the system changed over time.
23. As Daniel, I want clicking **"See the proof"** on a law (to view its tagged test around `@law: <id>`), clicking a broken law's drill-down (to view the failing CI log tail), or clicking a history commit's drill-down (to view its files/diff) to open an inline read-only drawer inside the Map view with one-click **"Open in editor"** / **"Open on GitHub"** links, so that I never lose my place on the map.
24. As Daniel, I want Home's row for a project to show one subtle mark (with no count) whenever a Core part is fogged or a law is broken, and clicking it to open that project's Map view, so that the map stays discoverable without turning Home into a dashboard.
25. As Daniel, I want a project with no `system-map.json` to say so clearly in the Map view and offer a **"Draft a map"** button that opens a new session in that project pre-filled with a drafting prompt, so that onboarding another repository is one click.
26. As Daniel, I want cards, Home items, and map surfaces to count as **Seen** only when they visibly intersect the viewport in a visible, focused window with their holding view open, so that off-screen or unfocused items are never miscounted as seen.
27. As Daniel, I want always-on stop-rule tracking (with no settings toggle and no score shown to me) that surfaces a quiet, dismissible one-time review after 14 active days and at least 20 merged PRs (whichever comes last) listing only what fell below its threshold — inside the Map view, and on Home too if the Map view itself missed its threshold — so that unused pieces can be pruned honestly.

## Implementation Decisions

### Visual craft and tokens
- **Treatment C (plates + cool-grey mist):** Build on Treatment A's plate geometry and surface hierarchy with a cool-grey mist token (`--mist`, around `#c4ccd6`, very low chroma) so fog and warm focus/brief light separate by temperature rather than hue. Add all map mist, light, and motion values to the design tokens file first so the raw-value token guard keeps passing.
- **Visual tuning carried from prototype review:**
  - Bump `--mist`'s alpha slightly over the prototype's C treatment so thin/lit fog reads cleanly under a warm ring without adding more blue.
  - Make the visual separation between **thin** and **thick** mist slightly clearer than the prototype's square-root curve (`0.45` → `0.67` vs `1.0`).
  - Keep `--conflict` and `--needs-you` unchanged; verify both colours side by side at small sizes in snap screenshots before shipping.
  - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` for mist drift, mist lift, and transitions.
- **No "Ready for review" tray in project 2:** Leave out the bottom-left PR brief tray until project 3 ships PR briefs, so nothing in the UI looks half-wired.

### Data source, default branch, and fog engine
- **Single commit of truth:** Read `system-map.json` directly from `origin`'s default branch ref as last fetched (`git show <default>:system-map.json`), and compute fog and part history from first-parent history on that same ref. If `origin/HEAD` is unset in a repository that was not cloned, fall back to the local default branch (`main`/`master`) with a quiet note.
- **Fetch triggers and guard:** Fetch `origin` when the Map view opens, when the window gains focus while it is open, and when Studio's landed-task check sees a task transition to merged — never on a timer. Guard `git fetch` with a per-repo cooldown (~60 s) and an in-flight lock so rapid focus switches never spam fetches or contend with worktree git operations; log fetch failures quietly.
- **In-memory matcher and historical map loading:** Add an in-memory entry point to `studio-system-map` that classifies paths against a parsed `Map` (rather than reading the working tree on disk). Keep strict `deny_unknown_fields` parsing for `system-map check` on HEAD, and add a lenient historical loader (ignoring unknown fields, degrading gracefully on unreadable commits) so future schema additions never break history scrubbing or fog walks.
- **Fog model:** Per project, store a fog state in the studio's data folder: the default-branch commit at which the project was first opened (so every project starts clear), and per-part lists of un-caught-up commits (each tagged `thin` or `thick`).
  - On refresh, walk new first-parent commits since the last processed commit. Classify each commit's changed paths against the **union** of the commit's map and its parent's map (so moving files between parts touches both source and destination).
  - Compare `system-map.json` between parent and commit to classify strength:
    - **Thick:** a law attached to the part, a link touching the part, a flow crossing the part, or the part's `paths` changed; or the part was newly added after first open.
    - **Thin:** internal files owned by the part changed, or only the part's `name`, `caption`, or `description` changed without structural changes.
    - **No fog:** `zone` changes (placement hint only), `ignored` changes, or **computed edge** changes (computed edges are hints for `system-map check`, never drawn on the map and never cause fog).
    - **Part removed:** dropped from the live map (its saved position/fog stays harmlessly in the store in case of revert) and still renders when scrubbing to earlier commits.
  - **"I know this"** clears a part's fog list, plays the mist-lift transition, and logs a dedicated stop-rule event.
- **Part positions and tiers:** Store Daniel's per-part tier overrides and `(x, y)` coordinates per part id in the studio's data folder (never in the repository).
  - **Tier precedence:** Daniel's local override always wins over `system-map.json`'s default `tier`. A repo change to `tier` applies only to parts without a local override. All fog filtering (`black-box` never fogs; `interface` fogs only `thick`) and Home's quiet mark (*"a Core part is fogged"*) use Daniel's **effective tier**.
  - Auto-place any part without a saved coordinate once (respecting links and optional `zone`, never moving already-placed parts). Support pointer dragging with a ~5–6 px movement threshold before entering drag mode so clicks to open a part sheet never nudge positions.

### Broken laws (CI on the default branch)
- **Triggering:** Query GitHub via `gh` for the latest finished run of the project's law-testing CI job on the default branch on the same triggers as fetch (map open, window focus while open, task seen as merged) — never on a timer. While a newer run is in progress, retain the last finished result and note in the drill-down that it is for an earlier commit.
- **Test-name attribution (not file-level):** Resolve each `@law: <id>` tag's `(file, line)` to the specific test function immediately following that comment (e.g. `fn <name>` in Rust, `test("<name>"` in Node). When the latest finished CI run failed, fetch its failed log via `gh`, parse failing test names from the supported test runners (`cargo nextest` and Node's test runner), match against tagged test names, and attach the coarse broken-law mark (*"a test that backs laws here failed on main"*) to the owning parts. Unrelated failing tests in the same file never trigger the mark.
- **Fail-quiet rule and status clarity:** Because `npm run check` runs as a `&&` chain and nextest uses default fail-fast, a missing red mark means only **"no known failure"**, not that every law test ran and passed. If CI failed before law tests ran (fmt, clippy, build), failed only in untagged tests, or the log cannot be fetched/parsed, show **no** broken-law red mark — and in the drill-down distinguish **"passed"**, **"law tests did not run"** (or unreadable log), and **"a test that backs laws here failed on main"**.

### Live agents and "not placed"
- Read active sessions and Workers from existing core state (`turn_trees` + active turn's changed files, plus Edit/Write paths while a turn is mid-flight). No new hook plumbing.
- Show only `Running` and `Needs you` sessions and Workers; Helpers and `Your turn` / `Idle` / `Ended` sessions never sit on the map.
- Place a session/Worker chip on **every** part its active turn touched. Active sessions with no changed files yet, `turn_trees: false`, status-only sessions, or `ignored`-only file changes appear in a quiet **not placed** list beside the map. Clicking any chip jumps straight to that session.

### History strip, inline proof, and drill-downs
- **History strip:** List first-parent commits on `origin/HEAD` touching the part's paths from the commit that introduced `system-map.json` onward (displaying PR number + title when present in the commit subject, else the commit summary). Scrubbing renders `system-map.json` as of that commit in a read-only mode (live agents and CI hidden, quiet *"Viewing `<commit>` · Back to now"* banner).
- **Inline proof and drill-downs:** Clicking **"See the proof"** on a law, a broken-law log link, or a history commit's files/diff opens a read-only drawer inside the Map view, with one-click **"Open in editor"** (using Studio's existing editor-open action) and **"Open on GitHub"** actions.
- **Layered Esc:** Scrubbed history → return to live; else open drill-down drawer → close drawer; else open part sheet → close sheet; else leave Map view.

### Shared `Seen` gate and stop-rule tracking
- **Shared `Seen` helper:** Build one viewport-observation helper requiring: element intersecting the viewport (**≥ 50% of the element OR ≥ 50% of the viewport**, so tall cards can still be seen) for ≥ 500 ms, document visible and window focused, and holding view active (`railShown`, `homeShown`, or `mapShown`).
  - Wire existing Story rail cards to this helper, fixing the built-is-shown bug where cards were marked shown on DOM creation. Note: changing what counts as shown introduces a one-time discontinuity in existing weekly guess rates (which retire in project 3); do not backfill or rewrite stored `shown` timestamps.
  - Use the same helper to record "offered in view" events for stop-rule tracking.
- **Stop rules (always on, no config, no scores):** Append structured usage events to a store in the studio's data folder. Evaluate per project once **both** conditions hold: **14 active days AND at least 20 merged PRs** (whichever comes **last**).
  - **Active day:** a local calendar day on which Studio had at least one session event or the Map view was opened.
  - **Thresholds:**
    - Map view: opened on ≥ 4 active days **or** on ≥ 20% of the active days on which Home's quiet mark was seen.
    - Part history strip: scrubbed ≥ 2 times.
    - "See the proof" / inline drill-downs: opened ≥ 2 times.
    - "I know this": recorded as its own event with no fail threshold in project 2 (baseline for project 3).
  - Surface a quiet, dismissible one-time review listing only modules below threshold inside the Map view — **and on Home too if the Map view itself missed its threshold**, so an unused map still reaches Daniel. Once dismissed, the review does not nag again while raw event logging continues quietly.

### Empty state and glossary
- **No-map project state:** When the selected project has no `system-map.json` on the default branch, render a calm empty state with a **"Draft a map"** button that launches Studio's existing New session flow in that project pre-filled with a drafting prompt referencing `system-map.json` and `system-map check`.
- **Glossary updates:** Fold the terms in `## Vocabulary` into `docs/studio/CONTEXT.md` in project 2's first ticket (self-contained from this spec, not relying on any unpushed local branch), and update `docs/studio/behaviour/map.md` as behaviour lands.
